skill.name: audio-transcriber
skill.description: Transcribe audio recordings into Markdown reports with metadata, timestamps, and optional AI-generated summaries.
skill.summary: Transcribe audio files into structured Markdown notes and summaries.
skill.author: Eric Andrade

security_audit.summary: Most static hits in Markdown and examples are false positives for fenced code, install instructions, or quoted metadata commands. Confirmed issues remain around automatic package installation, predictable temporary files, hidden home-directory probing, and sending transcripts to LLM CLIs. No prompt-injection text was found in the skill files, but transcript content is not isolated before LLM processing.

remediation.suggestion: Remove automatic pip installs from scripts/transcribe.py and require explicit dependency setup in a virtual environment.

remediation.issue: Transcript exposure to external LLM CLIs
remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit consent before Claude or GitHub Copilot processing, document cloud transfer, and add transcript-as-data guardrails.
Pass audio paths and model names through argv or environment variables, then parse them safely in Python.
Use configurable skill discovery or user-selected prompt tooling instead of checking ~/.copilot paths.
Use mktemp or Python tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile with restrictive permissions for intermediate transcription data.
Prefer a documented virtual environment workflow and avoid --break-system-packages unless the user explicitly opts in.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Transcripts Sent to LLM CLIs
semantic_findings.description: The Python workflow builds a prompt from transcript text and sends it to Claude or GitHub Copilot CLI. This can disclose sensitive audio content and lets transcript text act as LLM instructions without containment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly combines transcript text with the processing prompt and invokes cloud-backed LLM CLIs. The README also presents local privacy as a feature, which makes the external summary path important to disclose.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Variables Interpolated Into Python Source
semantic_findings.description: The example script expands AUDIO_FILE, MODEL, and TRANSCRIBER inside an unquoted Python heredoc. A crafted filename or environment value containing quotes could alter the generated Python source.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The heredoc is not quoted, so shell variables are expanded directly into Python string literals. The audio filename is user supplied, making code injection plausible.

content.value_statement: Audio reviews are slow when recordings must become clean notes. This skill transcribes audio into Markdown with metadata, timestamps, and optional summaries.
actual_capabilities: Detects Faster-Whisper or Whisper before transcription.
Extracts file size, duration, language, and segment timestamps.
Creates Markdown transcript and meeting-note files with timestamped names.
Can call Claude CLI or GitHub Copilot CLI for summaries.
Provides install scripts for Whisper, ffmpeg, rich, and tqdm.
limitations: Requires local Whisper or Faster-Whisper, and large models can be slow.
AI summaries may send transcript text to Claude or GitHub Copilot CLI.
The example script uses a predictable temporary file path.
Speaker labels are not robust diarization in the provided Python script.

prompt_templates.prompt: Transcribe workshop.flac and summarize product risks, unresolved questions, customer commitments, and next steps.

output: A Markdown transcript with file metadata and timestamped segments.
A meeting-note file with topics, decisions, action items, and summary paragraphs.

output_examples.input: Transcribe an interview without cloud AI processing.
output: A local transcript file with language, date, and timestamps.
No generated summary is created when AI processing is skipped.
A warning is shown for large files before processing continues.
The transcript is saved with a timestamped filename to reduce overwrites.

best_practices: Review privacy needs before enabling Claude or GitHub Copilot summary processing.
Use clear recordings and smaller Whisper models for faster first passes.
Store generated transcripts in a controlled output directory.
anti_patterns: Do not send confidential recordings to cloud LLM tools without approval.
Do not run dependency installers in shared environments without isolation.
Do not rely on automatic speaker labels for official attribution.

faq.question: Does this skill work offline?
faq.answer: Local transcription can work offline after dependencies and models are installed. AI summaries may require Claude or GitHub Copilot connectivity.

faq.question: Which audio engines are supported?
faq.answer: The provided scripts detect Faster-Whisper first, then OpenAI Whisper as a fallback.

faq.question: Can it create meeting minutes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create transcript files and optional meeting-note summaries when an LLM CLI is available.

faq.question: Does it upload audio files?
faq.answer: The Whisper transcription path is local. Summary generation can send transcript text to external LLM CLI services.

faq.question: What output format is most complete?
faq.answer: Markdown is the most complete path shown in the provided scripts and documentation.

faq.question: Is speaker diarization fully implemented?
faq.answer: The documentation describes speaker support, but the Python script mainly saves timestamped transcript segments.
